title: Yellowstone National Park
prompt: Plan me a first-time-friendly 3-day Yellowstone trip with wildlife, geyser basins, scenic stops, and no crazy hikes. Keep the pacing realistic.
description: Geysers, wildlife valleys and short canyon-rim walks with proper breaks.

images.alt: The sun sets behind the sharp point of a snow-covered mountain; pink clouds are reflected in a pond

plan.intro: Three full sightseeing days with short walks, assuming regular road-season access and a vehicle. Suggested base: Canyon Village, subject to availability. Day 1 focuses on geysers and colorful springs; Day 2 pairs Hayden Valley wildlife with short rim views of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone; Day 3 visits Lamar Valley and Mammoth terraces.

narrativeSections.heading: Practical notes
narrativeSections.markdown: Day 2 includes the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, anchored at Lookout Point with short rim views and an optional sidewalk section toward Grand View. Avoid steep descents such as Red Rock and Brink of the Lower Falls. Check [NPS road conditions](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm) for your dates: this is not a winter itinerary, and current access is unconfirmed. A vehicle is generally needed; there is no park-wide public transportation. Stay on thermal boardwalks and keep at least 100 yards from bears and wolves and 25 yards from other wildlife. Bring binoculars, layers, water and packed lunches.

plan.intro: Five full sightseeing days in mid-July, with arrival beforehand and departure afterward. narrativeSections.heading: Access and practical notes
narrativeSections.markdown: Mid-July does not guarantee snow-free alpine trails or an open Going-to-the-Sun Road. Check road status, trail closures and your travel year's vehicle-entry, Logan Pass parking and shuttle rules before committing. In 2026, Logan Pass shuttles required tickets and replaced the previous first-come system; do not assume those rules apply to another year. See [NPS shuttle information](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/shuttle-service-2026.htm). Hike distances are approximate and vary with starting point. Carry bear spray and know how to use it, keep wildlife distance, pack layers and rain protection, and avoid exposed terrain during thunderstorms. Book lodging early; availability and prices have not been confirmed. The two-base approach avoids repeated cross-park travel but requires one lodging move.

plan.parkName: Zion National Park, Bryce Canyon National Park, Capitol Reef National Park, Arches National Park, Canyonlands National Park
plan.intro: Seven days covering Zion National Park, Bryce Canyon National Park, Capitol Reef National Park, Arches National Park and Canyonlands National Park, including arrival from Las Vegas and departure toward Salt Lake City. The route assumes a vehicle and enough time on Day 1 to reach Springdale, with two nights in Springdale, one in Torrey and three in Moab. A full Zion canyon day leads into Bryce's amphitheater rim, a short Capitol Reef landscape-and-petroglyph morning, a close-up Turret Arch outing with a distant Delicate Arch view, and Canyonlands' Island in the Sky. These focused outings leave room for meals, transfers and recovery without strenuous hikes or extra stops. Dates, airport bookings and current access are unconfirmed. Road-time ranges are rough planning allowances, not confirmed routes; allow additional time for breaks, traffic and weather.

narrativeSections.heading: Before booking
narrativeSections.markdown:
The one-way Las Vegas–Salt Lake City route reduces backtracking but may carry a rental drop fee. Arrival must leave enough time to reach Springdale; for an early departure flight, add a Salt Lake City night rather than rushing from Moab. Day 3 is the longest combined sightseeing-and-driving day, with roughly 5–6 hours by road before breaks. Keep its Bryce rim outing modest and travel UT-12 in daylight when conditions allow. All transfer ranges are planning allowances; add parking, meals, traffic and weather delays.

Dates are unknown: confirm Zion Canyon shuttle rules, Arches entry requirements and all road and trail conditions. Bryce's seasonal shuttle is generally optional for ordinary-sized vehicles; larger vehicles have restrictions during shuttle hours ([NPS](https://www.nps.gov/places/000/bryce-canyon-shuttle-station.htm)). Summer favors early outings and afternoon rest; winter weather can affect Bryce and UT-12.

Capitol Reef's chosen morning pairs Panorama Point's layered landscape with the Petroglyph Panels viewing boardwalks before the move to Moab. At Arches, walk to Turret Arch and back, then see Delicate Arch from the lower, distant viewpoint—not via the strenuous hike to its base. Turret Arch involves steps and uneven surfaces with little shade. Carry food and water for park outings, and adjust walking to conditions and energy. The focused itinerary intentionally leaves afternoons for recovery rather than adding more attractions.

title: Acadia National Park
prompt: Plan a fall weekend in Acadia with sunrise, scenic drives, easy-to-moderate walks, and the best autumn atmosphere.
description: Sunrise, granite coast and autumn woodland with unhurried afternoons.

images.alt: A man and woman holding walking sticks hike up a mountain summit near a wooden trail sign.
images.credit: Photo courtesy of Sam Mallon, Friends of Acadia

plan.intro: Two full fall sightseeing days, assuming arrival Friday evening, a car available, and Bar Harbor as an unbooked base. Pair a conditional Cadillac sunrise and coastal scenic drive with a second day of woodland color and Jordan Pond. Dates and transportation are not confirmed; access depends on travel dates and conditions.

narrativeSections.heading: Fall logistics
narrativeSections.markdown: Early to mid-October is a useful foliage target, not a peak-color guarantee. Bring warm layers, rain protection and shoes with grip. A park entrance pass is required year-round; NPS says Cadillac Summit Road vehicle reservations apply from late May to mid-October—check exact dates and availability at https://go.nps.gov/AcadiaVehicleReservations. Road and trail conditions are not confirmed. Island Explorer has reduced fall service and a seasonal end date; check your year's schedule at https://www.nps.gov/acad/planyourvisit/island-explorer.htm rather than assuming buses serve your weekend or sunrise. If Cadillac access or weather fails, substitute coastal dawn at Ocean Path, combine that day's coastal walk with sunrise, and keep the breakfast/rest time.

stops.note: Enjoy the pond views and a shore walk. Allow about 2 hours for the fuller outing. Carry lunch; any seasonal dining service is unconfirmed.
stops.why: Combines water, mountain framing and autumn woodland without an exposed summit route.
